records.public_claim_text: OpenAI describes GPT-5.6 as a family of three models named Sol, Terra, and Luna.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: GPT-5.6 is a new family of three models: Sol, our new flagship model; Terra, a capable lower-cost option; and Luna, our fastest and most cost-efficient model.

records.public_claim_text: OpenAI reports that none of the three GPT-5.6 models reaches its High threshold for AI Self-Improvement.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: None of them reach our High threshold in AI Self-Improvement.

records.public_claim_text: OpenAI says GPT-5.6 training used public internet information, third-party-accessed information, and information provided or generated by users, trainers, and researchers.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: GPT-5.6 was trained on diverse datasets, including information that is publicly available on the internet, information that we partner with third parties to access, and information that our users or human trainers and researchers provide or generate.

records.public_claim_text: OpenAI says its challenging-prompt evaluations run without system-level safeguards.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Our evaluations are run on the model without system-level safeguards, to ensure the model’s underlying behavior meets our safety bar.

records.public_claim_text: OpenAI reports that the GPT-5.6 series performs generally on par with predecessors in its image-input safety evaluations and that minor regressions are not statistically significant.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: GPT-5.6 series performs generally on par with its predecessors. Minor regressions are not statistically significant.
